item.title: Watch: Linkin Park Drops "Over Each Other" Video as Controversy Looms Large

item.description: Jordan Mancino, the drummer who had been with As I Lay Dying since the early days, seems to have permanently checked out. Not in a quiet, amicable way either—this one comes with lawyers, statements, and all the usual mess you’d expect when band relationships implode.

item.title: Metallica's Kirk Hammett Declares Judas Priest the True Founders of Heavy Metal
item.description: Kirk Hammett isn’t here to play revisionist history with metal. When the drummer Carmine Appice tossed out the claim that heavy metal only began with Metallica, some folks had a field day.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Slipknot's Mask Maker Crafts Demonic Masks for Shin Megami Tensei V
item.description: Some collaborations leave you scratching your head, and this one’s no exception. Slipknot, the metal world’s masked enigma, has somehow found itself linked to Atlus, the studio behind the Shin Megami Tensei series.

item.title: Watch: As I Lay Dying Is Back: 'Burden' Released, Tour Announced
item.description: As I Lay Dying has returned with “Burden”, their first new single in five years, featuring their revamped lineup. The track introduces Ken Susi (ex-Unearth), Nick Pierce (ex-Unearth), and Ryan Neff (Miss May I), marking a new chapter for the band.

item.title: Slipknot’s Clown Misses Sonic Temple Due to Dental Surgery
item.description: Slipknot’s lineup has been feeling a bit like a revolving door lately, hasn’t it? Members coming, members going, and the occasional mystery replacement that leaves fans scratching their heads.

item.title: Slipknot Teases New Song Featuring Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Apparently, Slipknot has decided the best way to stay in the headlines is to sprinkle cryptic breadcrumbs all over the internet and let fans fight over the scraps.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING’s New Album Delayed: Tim Lambesis Explains Why
item.description: Tim Lambesis, AS I LAY DYING’s frontman, recently chatted on the Loaded Radio podcast about the band’s long-gestating new album. Apparently, the record’s been done for a while, but mixing has turned into a never-ending tug-of-war.

item.title: Jim Root: “Slipknot Is Lucky to Have Eloy Casagrande”
item.description: Slipknot’s Jim Root isn’t holding back his admiration for the band’s newest drumming powerhouse, Eloy Casagrande. If Root’s comments are anything to go by, it seems the band practically stumbled into the perfect fit without breaking a sweat—or even auditioning anyone else.

item.title: Slipknot Audition Secrets Revealed by Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Slipknot’s slow-drumroll announcement of Eloy Casagrande as their new drummer didn’t exactly shock anyone. Let’s be real, the fans had already connected the dots ages ago. Still, Eloy opened up in a recent chat with Veja São Paulo (in Portuguese), giving a blow-by-blow of his arduous audition experience.

item.title: Eloy Casagrande’s First Gig with Slipknot Leaves Fans in Awe
item.description: Slipknot’s newest recruit, Eloy Casagrande, hasn’t had much time to catch his breath. His debut as the band’s drummer wasn’t just any gig—it was a small, fiery show staged in a Californian desert venue that probably violates more safety codes than your local dive bar.

item.title: Slipknot Revives 1999 Look at Intimate Anniversary Show; VIDEO
item.description: In a tiny California venue better suited for a rowdy karaoke night than the launch of a metal juggernaut’s 25th anniversary, Slipknot made a dramatic entrance. Decked out in those bright red jumpsuits that defined their early days, the band treated the packed crowd at Pappy + Harriet’s in Pioneertown to a full-on blast from the past.

item.title: Evanescence's Amy Lee Responds to Linkin Park Vocalist Speculation
item.description: Amy Lee. Linkin Park. Together? (Ha, no.) But for a second, it almost felt real, didn’t it? All thanks to Jay Gordon (yes, from Orgy, of all people) who casually mentioned that Linkin Park might—might—be looking for a female vocalist.

item.title: Did Slipknot’s Website Just Confirm Their New Drummer?
item.description: Slipknot’s grand reveal of their mystery drummer is just days away, set to coincide with their live performance at Sick New World. But a few determined internet detectives might have already beaten the band to the punch.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Finalizes New Record Deal for 2024 Album
item.description: When Tim Lambesis sat down with Jamey Jasta on the “The Jasta Show”, the HATEBREED frontman probably knew he’d get some juicy tidbits on AS I LAY DYING’s new material.

item.title: Brian “Head” Welch Explains Korn’s Shift to Seven-String Guitars
item.description: Korn’s signature seven-string guitar sound didn’t start with some grand plan to revolutionize metal. No, it all began because James “Munky” Shaffer had a thing for Steve Vai, and Brian “Head” Welch?

item.title: Linkin Park Rumored to Return with a Female Lead Singer
item.description: July marks seven years since Chester Bennington’s untimely passing—a moment that shattered not just his family and friends, but the entire world of Linkin Park fans. His death wasn’t just tragic; it was a full stop.

item.title: Brian Welch on Korn's New Album: “The Heaviest in Years”
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch is dropping those familiar lines again—“heaviest stuff in years,” you know the drill. It’s almost like there’s a secret musician handbook, and on page one, right under “never say your best days are behind you,” is this classic line.

item.title: Korn’s Creative Process: Ray Luzier Breaks Down the Band’s Approach
item.description: Korn’s drummer, Ray Luzier, has been pounding the skins for the band since 2007, and he’s got plenty of stories to tell. In a chat with Modern Drummer, Luzier reflected on some of the band’s most memorable moments, from their biggest hits to their more out-there experiments.

item.title: Korn Announces 30th Anniversary Concert with Star-Studded Lineup
item.description: Korn isn’t one to let their 30th anniversary of that self-titled debut just slip by quietly. They’ve decided to throw a massive bash at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles on October 5, 2024.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Delays Album Completion Again; See Details
item.description: Here we are again, AS I LAY DYING has a new album brewing, but don’t hold your breath just yet. Vocalist Tim Lambesis, in an interview with Chaoszine, dished out the details, or at least as much as anyone could get from his roundabout explanations.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING's Tim Lambesis on New Album: “As Passionate as Ever”
item.description: Tim Lambesis, the ever-controversial voice behind AS I LAY DYING, let slip in a recent chat with the Today’s Boondoggle podcast that the band’s next studio album is set to land later this year (2024).

item.title: Metallica Wins Best Metal Performance, Only Trujillo Attends GRAMMYs
item.description: Metallica snags the Best Metal Performance GRAMMY, but if you think the band showed up in full force to accept it, think again. As usual, the GRAMMYs treated metal like an afterthought, burying the award for “72 Seasons” in the untelevised dungeon.

item.title: Korn’s Brian “Head” Welch Fights Back Against Mental Health Struggles
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist of Korn, has recently thrown himself into the mental health arena. He’s teamed up with Atlantic Behavioral Health, a fresh facility in Wilmington, Massachusetts.

item.title: Watch: Korn Meets Vanessa Carlton in a Bizarre Mashup
item.description: Just when you thought the world had run out of odd musical combinations, along comes YouTuber mac glocky with a new creation. Fresh off his last “masterpiece”—a mashup of System of a Down and the B-52s—he’s back with another experiment: what happens when you blend Vanessa Carlton’s early 2000s pop hit “A Thousand Miles” with the nu-metal force of Korn?

item.title: Korn's Brian Welch Introduces New Record Label XOVR Records; VIDEO
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist from Korn, has decided that making loud noises on stage wasn’t quite enough, so he’s now entering the record label world with his latest venture, XOVR Records (that’s “Crossover Records” for those who don’t speak in mysterious abbreviations).

item.title: Metallica Sets New Attendance Record at St. Louis Dome; See Details
item.description: Metallica has managed to once again defy expectations by packing out St. Louis’ Dome at America’s Center, showing that even after decades in the game, they’re still pulling crowds that could rival any pop superstar.

item.title: Metallica Competes for Billboard’s Top Rock Duo/Group Award
item.description: Metallica has snagged two Billboard Music Award nominations this year, a surprising nod from an awards scene that, let’s be honest, usually knows nothing about rock or metal.

item.title: MTV Names Metallica in Best Rock Category for EMA 2023
item.description: Metallica Earns a Nod for an MTV European Music Award—But Don’t Get Too Excited. Since the infamous moment when Jethro Tull snagged a Grammy over Metallica, metalheads everywhere learned that mainstream award shows are, for the most part, a waste of time.

item.title: Metallica’s Classic Albums Return in Limited Colored Vinyl Reissues
item.description: Metallica’s bringing out the big guns with their upcoming reissue series, serving up their classic albums on colored vinyl as if you haven’t bought these a few times already.

item.title: "Stream, Buy, or Steal": Lars Ulrich's Take on Modern Music Fans
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich once wore the crown of “public enemy” in the music scene, especially when he led the crusade against Napster and the whole file-sharing culture. Back then, he was the face of the so-called “greedy musician,” railing against the free-for-all nature of downloading that let everyone grab songs (and viruses) off the internet, slap them on a blank CD, and call it a day.

item.title: Korn's Next Album in 2024 Could Be Their First Without Fieldy
item.description: Korn apparently has some new sounds brewing for 2024, if guitarist Brian “Head” Welch is to be believed. He recently mentioned on The Joe Kingdom Perspective that there’s “new music coming next year,” though it seems like the band is in some kind of self-imposed exile right now, as he put it, “just doing our own thing.

item.title: Watch: Metallica Drops New “Too Far Gone?” Video with Tour Highlights
item.description: Metallica might’ve dropped 72 Seasons a mere five months back, but the internet reaction could’ve fooled anyone into thinking it’s been years since that release. One side hollered about “disastrous trash,” while the other shrugged, calling it “pretty decent.

item.title: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich on Tour, Streaming Records, and Band Longevity
item.description: Lars Ulrich is no stranger to marveling at Metallica’s unlikely ride to the top. As their colossal M-72 tour rolls on, the drummer recently shared some reflections with FOX 10, and let’s just say, humility is still in the air.

item.title: Metallica Welcomes Unlikely Guest: A Dog Named Storm at LA Concert
item.description: Los Angeles had an unexpected guest at Metallica’s August 25 concert—an adventurous dog named Storm who, without a ticket or invitation, managed to sneak into SoFi Stadium and settle right in with the crowd.

item.title: Metallica’s "Nothing Else Matters" Reaches 1 Billion Streams on Spotify
item.description: Metallica’s “Nothing Else Matters” has now crossed the monumental 1 billion streams mark on Spotify. This track, from the band’s blockbuster 1991 self-titled album, divides opinions like few others.

item.title: Metallica’s M72 Tour Breaks SoFi Stadium’s Single-Show Record
item.description: Metallica just sent Taylor Swift’s attendance record at SoFi Stadium spinning. In a double dose of pure metal, Metallica managed to pull off a weekend showdown that drew fans from every corner, making sure to leave their mark.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Begins Recording New Album With Fresh Lineup
item.description: The wheels are turning again for As I Lay Dying, and Tim Lambesis, the band’s infamous frontman, has confirmed their new album is officially in progress. Speaking with Heavy New York, Lambesis revealed that the group’s latest lineup is pulling its weight in the studio.

item.title: Amy Lee Reflects on Bring Me to Life's Rap: "Not My Style"
item.description: Amy Lee, the unmistakable voice of Evanescence, hasn’t minced words about her feelings toward the now-iconic rap segment in Bring Me to Life. For two decades, she’s openly expressed her discomfort with the label-driven decision to shoehorn in Paul McCoy’s rap—something neither she nor the band originally envisioned for their breakout hit.

item.title: Watch: Exclusive Footage of Metallica's Phantom Lord from Jon Zazula Tribute
item.description: Metallica just dropped official footage of them ripping through Phantom Lord at last weekend’s tribute show for their old manager, Jon Zazula. Yeah, it was one of those nights.

item.title: Watch: Metallica Pays Tribute to Megaforce Founders with Old-School Set
item.description: Metallica recently gave fans a nostalgic kick in the gut with a special throwback show that would make any old-school fan tear up—if they’re still capable of crying, that is.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Recruits Nick Pierce as Drummer for Tour; See Details
item.description: Jordan Mancino, the drummer who’s been part of As I Lay Dying since the beginning, has decided to step away from the band’s upcoming Two Decades of Destruction Tour.

item.description: The chaos surrounding As I Lay Dying just keeps piling up. After Josh Gilbert made his grand exit, the band scrambled to patch things together by roping in Ryan Neff of Miss May I to cover bass and vocals, while Ken Susi of Unearth stepped in on guitar.
